Date. April 15, 1935.
Subject N. I. Kovtunenko, suspected Soviet Agent.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [签名]
With reference to the endorsement of the Deputy
Commissioner (Special Branch) on the attached report regard-
ing N. I. Kovtunenko, enquiries show that this individual
is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in order
to work among the local White Russians as a Soviet agent-
provocateur, i.e. to collect information regarding the
anti-Bolshevik activities of Russian organizations and
private individuals and instigate the active "White" elements
to create incidents with a view to exposing local White Russians
to repressions on the part of the authorities. For this
purpose Kovtunenko posed as a "White," visited his former
friends who had known him as an officer of the "White" Army,
visited restaurants etc. frequented by "White" Russians and
made an attempt to join the Union of Former Cadets of the
Vilno Military School.
[签名]
D. S.
Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)

关于附呈报告中涉及 N. I. Kovtunenko 一事，经副警司（特别处）批注后，经查询得知，据报此人从哈尔滨抵达上海，旨在作为苏联挑衅性特工在当地白俄人群中开展工作，即收集有关俄国组织及个人反布尔什维克活动的情报，并煽动活跃的“白俄”分子制造事端，以期使当地白俄人士遭受当局的镇压。为此目的，Kovtunenko 伪装成“白俄”，拜访了他以前在“白军”服役时结识的朋友，光顾白俄人士常去的餐馆等场所，并试图加入维尔诺军事学校前学员联合会。
[签名]

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY. File No. 6-17 No. D 6-17 Br. xxxxxxxx / 25）
Date March 30, 1935.

Subject N. I. Kovtunenko, suspected Soviet Agent.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by DBRm 3/1.

（批：S2 Please explain the line of work on which he is engaged as an agent. JMS）
（批：DS Tcheremshansky OAB 1/4.）

Information has been received that Nicolay Ignatievitch
Kovtunenko, 37, Russian, residing at No. 228 Route Vallon,
is suspected of being a Soviet Agent. He arrived in
Shanghai a few months ago and on 11.3.35 registered with the
local Public Safety Bureau as a Soviet citizen.
It is reported that in 1916 Kovtunenko graduated from
the Vilno Military School for Officers and that he saw
active service during the Great War. In 1919 or 1920 he
appeared in Harbin. Two years later he became a Soviet
citizen, following which he obtained employment with the
Educational Department of the Chinese Eastern Railway.
While in Harbin, he published a pro-Soviet magazine entitled
"Youth". In 1928 Kovtunenko in partnership with Safariantz
and K.I. Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky, Soviet citizens, bought over
the "OZO" printing establishment (formerly owned by the
Union of ex-Officers of Transamur Military District). It
is reported that that enterprise was financed by the Far
Eastern Bank (Dalbank) and that it printed text-books for
Soviet Schools as well as stationery etc. for the Chinese
Eastern Railway.
In Shanghai Kovtunenko posed as a White Russian. In
February 1935 he made an unsuccessful attempt to join the
Union of Former Cadets of the Vilno Military School. At the
same time he was seen visiting the U.S.S.R. Consulate-General.
On February 21, 1935, Kovtunenko was present at the Shanghai
& Hongkew Lower Wharf at the time of departure for Vladivostok
of the Soviet s.s. "Sever," on board which vessel his former
partner and friend, Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky, was leaving for
the U.S.S.R.

日期 1935年3月30日。

事由 N. I. Kovtunenko，涉嫌苏联特工。

撰写人：D.S. Tcheremshansky 转呈人：DBRm 3/1。

（批：S2 请说明其作为特工从事的工作性质。JMS）
（批：DS Tcheremshansky OAB 4月1日。）

接获情报称，Nicolay Ignatievitch Kovtunenko，37岁，俄国人，居住于华伦路（Route Vallon）228号，涉嫌为苏联特工。他于数月前抵达上海，并于1935年3月11日向当地公安局登记为苏联公民。
据报，Kovtunenko 于1916年毕业于维尔诺军官军事学校，并在第一次世界大战期间服现役。1919年或1920年，他出现在哈尔滨。两年后，他成为苏联公民，随后在中东铁路教育部任职。
在哈尔滨期间，他出版了一份亲苏杂志，名为《青年》。1928年，Kovtunenko 与苏联公民 Safariantz 和 K.I. Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky 合伙，收购了“OZO”印刷所（原由外阿穆尔军区前军官联合会所有）。据报，该企业由远东银行（Dalbank）提供资金，印制苏联学校的教科书以及中东铁路的文具等用品。
在上海，Kovtunenko 伪装成白俄。1935年2月，他试图加入维尔诺军事学校前学员联合会，但未成功。与此同时，有人看见他访问苏联总领事馆。1935年2月21日，苏联轮船“Sever”号从上海及虹口下码头启程前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），Kovtunenko 当时在场，他的前合伙人兼朋友 Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky 正乘坐该船前往苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟。

The latter individual was a member of the Narodnoe
Sobranie (People's Assembly) of the Maritime Province in
1920-22 when that province was under a "White" regime.
During this period Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky claimed to be Chair-
man of the "All Russian Farmers' Union" and was suspected of
being a Soviet agent. Later, in Harbin, he obtained a
Soviet passport and was connected with the Soviet administrat-
ion of the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Recently Kovtunenko was questioned by one of his
friends regarding the nature of his connections with
Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky. He admitted that he had been a
Soviet citizen since 1922 and that he had the intention of
returning to Soviet Russia, in connection with which matter
he had visited the local Soviet Consulate on three occasions.
G. Tcheremshansky.
D. S.

后者曾在1920-22年间滨海边疆区处于“白俄”政权统治时期担任该地区的 Narodnoe Sobranie（人民议会）成员。在此期间，Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky 自称是“全俄农民联盟”主席，并被怀疑是苏联特工。后来，在哈尔滨，他获得了苏联护照，并与中东铁路的苏联管理部门有联系。
最近，Kovtunenko 的一位朋友就其与 Ziplenkoff-Slaviansky 关系的性质向他提出质问。他承认自1922年以来一直是苏联公民，并有意返回苏维埃俄国，为此事他曾三次访问当地苏联领事馆。
G. Tcheremshansky。
